lead: Baltimore plumbing deals with century-old rowhouses, aging sewer laterals and cold winters. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Baltimore.
risk: old galvanized and lead pipes, basement sewer backups and frozen pipes
risk_short: old pipes, sewer backups and frozen pipes
why: Baltimore's rowhouses often date from before 1940, with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and old sewer laterals. Tight basements and shared walls make repairs slow.
Heavy storms back up sewers into basements in older neighborhoods. Winters freeze pipes in exterior walls and vacant houses.
utility: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
water: Baltimore's water comes from the Loch Raven, Liberty and Prettyboy reservoirs, with the Susquehanna River as a backup source. The water is relatively soft. Homeowners are responsible for their private sewer lateral and the service line on their side.
tips: Insulate basement and wall pipes before winter.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Know where your shutoff is; often in the front basement.
Scope the sewer lateral before buying.
areas: PipeMend works in Canton, Fells Point, Federal Hill, Hampden, Roland Park, Highlandtown, Mount Vernon and every other Baltimore neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits in Baltimore are issued through the city's Department of Housing and Community Development, and plumbers must be licensed by the Maryland State Board of Plumbing.

faq.a: The Maryland State Board of Plumbing licenses plumbers and gas fitters statewide. Permits for work in Baltimore come from the city.
